source_scope.lane: historical Retina/adaptive-vision lineage -> FrankEye -> frozen Digital Retina source -> FRANK 0.1 Micro Visual Classifier requirement

dedup_decisions: SOMA adaptive-LoRA lifecycle and Project Engine autonomy are already covered by the peer receipt and receive no duplicate credit here.
This shard is limited to visual perception lineage and the distinction between adaptive routing/inference and user-adaptive visual learning.

findings.claim: The historical module named frank_adaptive_vision.py was adaptive primarily in compute routing: Stage 1 fast YOLO/OCR/scene analysis always ran, an EscalationEngine decided whether Stage 2 Ollama VLM was needed, and the service combined the two paths. Its verified deletion patch does not establish a persistent user-specific visual learner, prototype memory, trusted-example admission, or cyclic classifier training.
findings.implication: Do not count the historical 'adaptive vision' name as evidence that the FRANK 0.1 Micro Visual Classifier requirement was already implemented. Reuse the cheap-first/escalate-on-uncertainty control pattern only.

findings.claim: Commit 0fd27f23 replaced frank_adaptive_vision.py and frank_visual_pipeline.py with a 937-line FrankEye module. FrankEye explicitly merged Digital Retina v8 CNN classification, DINOv2 scene analysis, GOLPU features, OCR and face detection into a CPU-only pipeline; the Retina CNN section is explicitly inference-only.
findings.implication: The historical consolidation is strong evidence for dissolving perception into one fast pipeline, but not for online personal learning.

findings.claim: The frozen Digital Retina source describes itself and implements its public API as stateless image analysis. It runs reusable visual models and returns structured concepts/objects/OCR/faces/scene output, but retina/core.py contains no durable per-user classifier state or update contract in the public analyze path.
findings.implication: User-specific familiarity must be represented as an explicit stateful layer/plane integrated with dissolved Retina semantics, rather than silently attributed to the stateless sensor service.

findings.claim: The fixed FRANK 0.1 directive correctly fills the historical gap: frozen reusable visual features feed an adaptive Micro Visual Classifier with calibrated known/unknown/conflict routing, trusted GOLD/SILVER admission, bounded cyclic updates, candidate shadow evaluation, rollback and replay. This is additive to the verified stateless Retina lineage and must not conflate familiarity with sensor truth.
findings.implication: Preserve the cheap-first historical routing lesson, reuse frozen features already computed by Retina, and keep learned familiarity state versioned/provenanced so H1/H2/H3 can differentially replay it.

findings.claim: The Drive Digital Retina tracked source identity is frozen at 241 tracked leaves, but untracked/generated/model/support material and the separate 64-leaf E2E evidence lineage remain distinct reconciliation obligations. Therefore this shard cannot close the whole Digital Retina Drive subtree or award global exact Level-0 coverage.

negative_results.result: No verified persistent user-specific visual familiarity learner was found in the inspected historical frank_adaptive_vision -> FrankEye transition or in the frozen Digital Retina public stateless API path.
negative_results.meaning: This is a scope-bounded negative result, not proof that no such mechanism exists anywhere else in the 241 tracked leaves or untracked Drive material.
negative_results.next_falsifier: Find a versioned persistent per-user prototype/readout/training-buffer implementation elsewhere in the frozen Digital Retina or Project-Frankenstein lineage and reconcile it into this receipt.

earned_work_mapping.reason: The cheap-first/escalation and frozen-feature mechanisms are historically useful, but existing visual/architecture mappings may overlap. This receipt records mechanism evidence without inflating provisional avoided-hours totals.
